evidence.field: 南 entry; graphic history and explanation
evidence.text: The entry labels 南 a loan graph (假借字). It presents Shang forms as an independent pictograph, with the original meaning unknown, and reports that the graph was borrowed for the direction word in Yin-period oracle-bone inscriptions, citing Heji 9738. It also reports a later extension for southward movement and a use for music of ancient southern peoples. The author rejects the received Shuowen component analysis: in the printed clause, 南 is analyzed 从𣎵、𦍒(rěn)聲 and said to be unconvincing. The printed sound referent is 𦍒, not OCR’s 𦍑; the entry does not establish a sound or semantic component analysis for current 南. It cites transmitted texts for later uses but does not date those uses or establish the chronology of the word senses.
evidence.title: 字源 (李學勤主編, 2012)

evidence.field: 南 entry; chart and variant account
evidence.text: The chart labels forms from Shang, Western Zhou, Warring States, Qin, Han, small seal and clerical script. The prose describes later graphic change and confusion with 市-like forms, after which one form fell out of use. These are the book’s chart and account; they do not by themselves establish a continuous derivation from a particular Shang object picture.

evidence.source: Huang Bo, 《甲骨文“南”及相关字补说（上）》, hosted by Fudan University Center for Research and Preservation of Excavated Texts via LingLab; inspected article text, abstract, form groups and discussion of prior proposals.
evidence.field: Abstract and sections I–III; oracle-bone forms, uses, and competing interpretations
evidence.text: Huang argues that the Shang graph was the original graph for 醓, a meat sauce, and depicts a covered cylindrical vessel with a plant-like feature above. He reviews instrument, animal-young and helmet readings, and reports oracle-bone uses for direction, the ancestor name 南庚, and a sacrificial item. The sacrificial-item reading remains disputed in the article; Huang’s 醓 analysis is an argued proposal, not settled consensus, and the reported uses do not establish their semantic order.
evidence.title: 《出土文献》 | 黄博：甲骨文“南”及相关字补说（上）

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of Information Science, Chinese Character Database; inspected 南 form-history entry.
evidence.text: The database presents the instrument-origin account: 南 originally named a musical instrument, its upper part indicated a hanging portion, and the graph was later borrowed for south. This is an institutional database’s interpretation and conflicts with the vessel proposal reviewed by Huang Bo; it does not settle the original referent.
evidence.title: 漢字「南」：字形演變

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants; inspected 南 entry.
evidence.field: 南 entry; received Shuowen analysis, dictionary senses and historical citations
evidence.text: The entry records the received Shuowen analysis as 从𣎵、𢆉聲, identifies 𡴖 as an ancient form in that account, and gives senses including south, southward movement, and a southern musical mode with transmitted textual citations. This documents the received dictionary account and later lexical tradition; it does not establish Shang word-sense chronology or independently settle the graph’s original formation.
